summary: This paper proposes a continuous-variable gate-based quantum Boltzmann machine implemented with Gaussian photonic gates, ancilla measurements, and variational QITE, and evaluates it on SAR image distributions and quantum-state targets. Reported results include 99.8% fidelity with KL divergence 0.006 for forest SAR data, 98.9% and 0.013 for sea-ice SAR data, 96.1%/98.1%/91.4% fidelities for Rayleigh/Gamma/ET-IB distributions, and 99.55% and 98.22% fidelities for Gaussian and cat-state quantum data, respectively.

experiments.description: CVQBM trained and evaluated on classical SAR image intensity distributions for forest monitoring in Acre, Brazil.

problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize fidelity F(rho_data, rho_v) and minimize cost C = 1 - F
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: post-selection on ancilla qumode measurement outcome n=1 at each QITE step
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: effective Hamiltonian Heff(zeta) defined implicitly by rho_v = exp(-Heff(zeta))
